Hi Alice —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap of what we heard on the call and proposed next steps so we can align with your security and privacy team:

Summary of requirements:
- No persistent storage of user PII or conversation transcripts (0-retention) for specific endpoints used in fraud-detection workflows.
- Shortened operational logs (7-day rolling) for metrics/alerts only; redact any PII from logs.
- Data residency: customer data must remain in us-east-1.
- Audit/logging controls: need proof of deletion and an option for on-demand purge.

Next steps we suggested:
1) I'll scope what's feasible with our serving/runtime team and Rafael on feasibility/impact to observability and SLOs.
2) We'll share a proposed exception workflow and an exception request form for Legal.
3) If acceptable, we'll draft a service addendum and route to DocuSign.

Can you confirm the list above matches what your privacy team needs and whether Legal wants any additional artifacts (SOC2 evidence, deletion certificate format)?

Thanks — aiming to get back with an internal proposal by early next week.

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap — that captures it well. To add a few specifics from Legal/Privacy:
- For our fraud workflow we cannot allow storage of raw transcripts or PII beyond real-time inference — effectively 0-retention for those endpoints.
- Operational metrics (latency, error counts) are fine with a 7-day retention but logs must be scrubbed of PII before being persisted.
- We will need a written deletion certificate for any ad-hoc purge requests within 48 hours of completion.

If you can propose concrete implementation options (e.g., routing to ephemeral-only model instances, disabling KV cache persistence, or per-customer retention flags) and an expected impact to latency/SLA, we can take that to Legal for approval.

Also: please CC our LegalOps mailbox (legal@fintechcap.com) on the exception request doc.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — this is a gating item for our procurement timeline.

Hi Alice / LegalOps —

Thanks for the patience while we evaluated options. Attached is our proposed exception package and implementation plan (see attached PDF + spreadsheet). High-level proposal:

- Scope: 0-retention for the named fraud-detection endpoints (no transcript or raw PII persisted).
- Operational logs: 7-day retention window for scrubbed metrics; PII redaction applied client-side and again at ingestion.
- Purge & certificates: We will provide an automated purge tool for customer-initiated deletions; our infra team will produce a deletion certificate within 48 hours of the purge completing.
- Data residency: Instances pinned to us-east-1 for this tenant.
- Exceptions governance: 6-month pilot review, after which we will either graduate to standard policy or renew the exception with a security review.

Rafael confirmed feasibility with a small tradeoff: ephemeral-only routes add ~3–7ms median latency for the endpoints and will reduce telemetry granularity (we’ll surface aggregated metrics and synthetic checks to preserve SLO monitoring).

Next steps:
1) FinTech Legal to review attached exception form (redwood-data-retention-exception-form.pdf). Please CC legal@fintechcap.com on any updates.
2) If accepted, we'll send a DocuSign addendum (link below) for signature and provision the tenant in us-east-1 with the pilot settings.
3) Rafael / Infra will coordinate a 1-hour tech kick-off to validate purge workflows and certificate delivery.
